lockup.summary: The company, its officers, directors and nearly all other holders agreed not to sell shares for 180 days after the prospectus date, unless the lead underwriters agree in writing. Nearly all shares then become eligible for sale.

what: Develops stem cell therapies, made from each patient's own cells, to treat Parkinson's disease and other brain diseases.
proceeds: It expects to raise about $125.8 million after costs. It plans to spend about $110.0 million on a Phase 3 trial of its Parkinson's treatment, $8.0 million on the current trial and $4.0 million on early-stage research, with the rest for general costs.
risks: It is a young company with no approved products, so it is hard to judge its approach or its future.
It has lost a lot of money since it started and may never make a profit.
Its financial condition raises serious doubt about whether it can keep operating.
Even after this offering, it will need a lot more money, and may have to cut or stop programs without it.
Raising more money could dilute shareholders, limit how it operates, or force it to give up rights to its technology.
